content.text: The text combines polemical accounts condemning Roman Catholicism with numerous narratives of persecution, torture, imprisonment, forced confession, convent abuse, and escape. It describes Inquisitions in Lower Canada, Spain, Goa, Macerata, Rome, and elsewhere: victims are confined in cells, examined in torture chambers, paraded in autos-da-fé, or executed. Dellon is imprisoned in Goa, later marched through the city and sent to the galleys; Buchanan visits the Goa Inquisition but is refused access to its dungeons. A Macerata counsellor arrests Count della Torre at home; the count dies after torture, while the counsellor flees Italy through Switzerland to England. Other alleged escapees flee convents in Bohemia and Naples. The text then shifts to poems about love, death, desire, war, disease, and exile, before ending with an Arkansas family saga involving Cousin Cæsar, Roxie Daymon, inheritance, deception, and a Chicago lawyer.
